method: Each symbol's interior was isolated by flood-filling from a seed point inside its closed outline, which excludes the attached inflow, outflow and heat-sink arrows. The aspect ratio is the width over the height of that interior region. Measured by tests/fidelity/measure_reference.py; rerun it rather than editing these numbers by hand.
precision: The reference is a 144 DPI capture in which symbol interiors span 31-107 px. A one-pixel error on the smaller dimension is therefore worth 1-3%. Tolerances below are set no tighter than that measurement precision justifies, and a symbol whose tolerance is wider says why.

source.note: circle; measures round, which validates the extraction

storage.note: tank; peak height is sensitive to stroke width at this DPI

consumer.note: hexagon pointed top and bottom; shoulders at 0.46 of half-height

transaction.note: exchange diamond; at 31 px tall the reference's own 2-3 px stroke consumes much of the interior, which caps the achievable overlap -- hence the lowest threshold here

interaction.note: pointed right, notched left; 35 px of height limits precision

gain.note: constant-gain amplifier; 33 px wide makes this the least precise

loop_limited.note: body taller than wide; the style's minimum width/height ratio sets this

switch.note: switching action; all four sides bowed inward

iou_method: Interior-region overlap: each symbol's enclosed region is isolated (by flood fill for the reference, by filling the outline for the render), normalised to a 512x512 square, and compared by intersection over union. Interiors rather than outlines, so the measure is independent of stroke weight -- which differs between a 144 dpi capture and a vector render and is not what conformance asks about.
iou_calibration: iou_min is the measured agreement less 0.05, so a threshold reflects what this symbol pair actually achieves rather than a guess. Re-run measure_reference.py and re-derive rather than loosening a threshold to make a failure go away.
height_ratio_method: Height of the bare symbol divided by the bare producer's, against the same ratio measured from Odum's sheet. This is what the grid exists to guarantee: each shape grows from its label at its own rate (producer 2.0x the text half-height, consumer 3.23x, gain 5.2x), so without a common floor identical labels give wildly different symbols. \energeseunit sets that floor per symbol; this invariant checks it still holds.
